full_judgment: 24. The General Rule of interpretation is that if a provision contains direction respecting the time or modes of proceeding for exercise of power, there is at least a strong presumption that the power must be exercised in that time and mode. This time factor and mode of proceeding gives a provision a mandatory nature. Further the use of expression 'shall' in a provision, in general be always taken to be indicative of its mandatory nature, but not, if the neglect of the main object of the provision does not affect the validity of the acts done. In such a case the provision should be held to be directory. What we find in Articles 123 is not only the use of the expression 'shall' but also a time limit of ninety days, within which the election for a seat fallen vacant causally, is to be' held. Therefore there is little scope for controversy that this Article is not meant to be mandatory by the legislature.
